summary: All 274 tests pass (0 failures). WP-011 adds 17 integration tests for branch-orchestrator.ts using real local git repositories. All 5 acceptance criteria met: (1) npm test passes, (2) tests use a local origin repo with pre-created branches (buildOrigin()), (3) switchBranches creates new branches when they don't exist, (4) DateModified is updated after switch operations including partial failures, (5) per-repo result structure verified with multi-repo tests checking result.results keys.

comments.note: Edge case: switchBranches with nonexistent repo path reports success=false with error string — verified.
Edge case: DateModified is updated even on partial failure (nonexistent repo) — verified.
Edge case: conflict detection on git checkout with local modifications — test verifies either conflict=true or error is set.

summary: WP-011 code review PASS. Both branch-orchestrator.ts (source) and branch-orchestrator.test.ts (tests) reviewed line-by-line. Architecture is well-designed: constructor-injected dependencies, clean separation of private repoPath() helper from public API, correct concurrent Promise.all patterns, elegant case-insensitive deduplication in compileBranchSuggestions(). Test suite is exemplary — real git integration tests with deterministic local fixtures, proper process.on('exit') cleanup, 17 tests covering all branches of logic including multi-repo, conflict detection, and DateModified guarantees. No blocking issues. Two documentation-forward items tagged for the Documentation agent (switchBranches missing @throws annotation, conflict test assertion comment).

comments.note: No improvement needed — branch-orchestrator.test.ts already implements process.on('exit') cleanup with fs.rmSync(tmpRoot, { recursive: true, force: true }). This is the reference pattern the WP-003 fix-forward was modelled on.

[documentation-forward] switchBranches() in src/orchestration/branch-orchestrator.ts does not validate project/workspace existence before iterating branchAssignments, unlike getAvailableBranches() which throws when the project is not found. Add a @throws annotation (or inline comment) to switchBranches() JSDoc clarifying that the workspace must exist and that an invalid projectId/workspaceId will propagate an error from the workspaceManager.update() call only after all per-repo operations complete.

[documentation-forward] The conflict-detection test assertion (`conflict === true || error !== undefined`) is intentionally permissive because git output varies across versions and platforms; document this explicitly in the test comment so future maintainers don't tighten it without understanding the cross-platform variance.

compileBranchSuggestions() remote prefix normalisation uses branch.name.indexOf('/') + 1, which correctly strips only the first remote prefix regardless of forward slashes in the branch name itself (e.g. origin/feature/x -> feature/x). Clean implementation.

summary: Documentation pass for WP-011 (Branch Orchestrator Tests). Three changes made: (1) Added @throws annotation to switchBranches() JSDoc in branch-orchestrator.ts clarifying that project/workspace existence is not validated up front and that errors surface only from workspaceManager.update() after all per-repo operations complete. (2) Added cross-platform variance comment to conflict-detection test assertion in branch-orchestrator.test.ts explaining why the permissive assertion is correct. (3) Added 'Branch orchestrator' section to README.md documenting the BranchOrchestrator constructor, all three public methods (getAvailableBranches, compileBranchSuggestions, switchBranches), return types, error behaviour, and conflict-detection design note. Both documentation-forward items from code review were addressed.

comments.note: Addressed both documentation-forward items from code review: switchBranches @throws annotation added, and conflict-detection assertion comment added to test. README BranchOrchestrator section covers all public API surface including conflict-detection caveat note.
